scope: Twenty selected actual-content guides with specifically scoped credited pictures.

profiles.name: Chehalis
remainingGaps: Review Upper and Lower Chehalis communities and other named constituent groups individually before adding relationships or distinct government routes.
Add dated community-authored history and language publications beyond these institutional introductions.
Consult original historical records separately before adopting explorer dates or outsiders’ labels.

profiles.name: Clallam
remainingGaps: Review Port Gamble and appropriate other S’Klallam community publications individually, without automatic affiliation or alias assumptions.
Original deeds, treaty records, fuller language publications and later timeline entries remain unreviewed.

profiles.name: Colville
remainingGaps: Develop separate historical reading paths for the Colville people and other constituent peoples without treating a confederated institution as every community’s voice.
Read selected tribal historical publications and original records; the linked story-map introduction and multimedia works were not inspected here.
Review actual language teaching materials separately and retain speaker/community scope.

profiles.name: Cowlitz
remainingGaps: Add dated language-program publications and independently inspect selected teaching resources.
Compare Engdahl’s historical interpretation with original records and scholarship while retaining uncertainty around historical names.
Review the legacy county-hosted cultural-report card’s authorship and perspective; its old Indigenous-led classification has not been validated by this batch.

profiles.name: Duwamish
remainingGaps: Add dated community publications and selected original historical records beyond institutional introductory pages.
Review linguistic scholarship and teaching materials separately; do not infer disappearance from language change.
Inspect recognition-related primary decisions separately before making current legal statements, with other relevant community perspectives clearly distinguished.

profiles.name: Kwakwaka'wakw
remainingGaps: Review individually named community histories and contemporary language publications without treating the broader label as one government.
Museum objects, family-held knowledge, designs and recordings require separate study and permissions.

profiles.name: Lummi
remainingGaps: Review selected complete community-plan culture pages and later community-led language/history publications; later PDF culture-context retrieval timed out.
Check later educational/program histories without carrying 2022 figures forward as current.

profiles.name: Makah
remainingGaps: Read selected community-approved archaeological and language publications; no excavation report or individual museum object was reviewed here.
Keep museum interpretation and current political/legal questions distinct.

profiles.name: Nooksack
remainingGaps: Read selected linguistic and historical scholarship with the original records cited by the Tribe.
Inspect technical monitoring and habitat reports before reporting measurable environmental outcomes.
Review distinct family/community perspectives and contemporary governance questions carefully; introductory institutional history is not an enrollment or legal determination.

profiles.name: Nuu-chah-nulth
remainingGaps: Develop separate, community-directed histories and language reading paths across the distinct nations.
Inspect original organizational and land-protection records before expanding institutional or legal claims.
Compare community evaluations of stewardship without treating stated goals or counters as demonstrated ecological outcomes.

profiles.name: Puyallup
remainingGaps: Read original records and further Puyallup-authored histories before extending treaty, settlement or current legal claims.
Follow community-directed evaluations of language learning rather than adopting reported speaker totals as a current census.
The 2021 heritagePDF is a directory of leads, not a separately inspected history; linked videos remain unwatched.
Retain the earlier language-site URL with explicit access caution; do not present its anomalous footer as evidence about the institution itself.
The modern industrial river-mouth aerial is regional place context, not reconstructed former villages or a reservation boundary.

profiles.name: Quileute
remainingGaps: Review appropriate fuller histories, community-approved language publications and present educational work without inferring disappearance from language loss.
Linked lessons, recordings, dictionary and historic claims about other peoples remain separately unreviewed.

profiles.name: Quinault
remainingGaps: Review later community-led Taholah updates, constituent-community histories and language works.
Later construction status, hazard studies and present agency policies remain unverified.

profiles.name: Skokomish
remainingGaps: Broaden community-authored Twana language and family history beyond two institutional accounts.
Inspect original river, dam and land records alongside tribal histories before making legal, environmental-outcome or current access claims.
Do not convert historical Twana community names into separate present governments without identity-specific evidence.
Archive responsibilities are not permission to reproduce cultural objects or sensitive records; seek only appropriate public sources.

profiles.name: Snoqualmie
remainingGaps: Read original recognition documents and compare selected community-authored histories.
Expand language and family perspectives without reproducing restricted knowledge or assuming one account speaks for everyone.
Inspect primary land/planning records before adding boundaries, current ownership or later outcomes.

profiles.name: Squaxin Island
remainingGaps: Read original treaty and agency records alongside community histories before extending chronology or legal conclusions.
Add individually attributed family and inlet-community perspectives; do not automatically treat historical labels as present governments.
Verify current island access and visitor conditions independently rather than repeating undated webpage rules.
Review actual public museum publications and language sources; a description of collections is not inspection or reuse permission.

profiles.name: Suquamish
remainingGaps: Read original treaty and land records alongside Suquamish interpretations before making legal or boundary claims.
Broaden family and community-authored language and historical scholarship beyond these two institutional accounts.
Review current programmes separately; undated descriptions do not establish present outcomes.
The wharf image is a historical place view with conflicting catalogue dates, not a named-member or Indigenous-vessel portrait.

profiles.name: Tulalip
remainingGaps: Add individually scoped histories from constituent communities rather than treating one institutional narrative as every person’s experience.
Read original school, government and land records before extending chronology or legal conclusions.
Verify current educational outcomes and visitor conditions independently; the selected guide is not a live schedule.
The dated Priest Point view is regional place context; its camera is described as at a cemetery, but no graves or markers are visible. No access or territorial claim follows.

profiles.name: Samish
remainingGaps: Inspect selected original historical records, linguistic studies and Nation-published archive material.
Read the linked environmental reports and data before assessing monitoring results or restoration outcomes.
Review Samish legal-history primary documents separately; do not merge the Nation with neighboring Coast Salish governments or every historical descendant.

profiles.name: Stillaguamish
remainingGaps: Read original acknowledgement and land records before extending recognition chronology, jurisdiction or boundary claims.
Broaden Stillaguamish-authored language, family and environmental history, retaining individual speakers and periods.
Check later departmental accounts before reporting current activities or measured outcomes.
The Chief Seattle-attributed quotation on the department page was not used; its provenance needs separate verification.
South Fork river image is a modern landscape setting, not a reconstruction of a named historical village or a present reservation boundary.

sourceCounting: 23 appended profile-source contexts and 22 same-ID/same-URL card updates, including explicit excluded/supporting metadata corrections. Shared/reused publications are not globally new works. Identity-only evidence excluded.
provenance: Selected scopes/dates and media-specific creator/source/rights/complete-available-frame limits retained. No private files or full third-party texts published.
